skill.name: context-management
skill.description: Context management guidance for multi-agent workflows, long-running tasks, session handoffs, memory workflows, and project state preservation.
skill.summary: Capture, compress, and hand off project context across AI-assisted workflows.
skill.author: Joseph OBrien

security_audit.summary: Most static command-execution and reconnaissance alerts are false positives caused by Markdown fences and workflow prose. The filesystem artifact pattern is a real moderate risk because it uses shared /tmp paths and broad glob collection. A semantic review also found credential-retention guidance that needs stronger secret-handling safeguards.

remediation.suggestion: Remove credentials from the list of information to preserve, or require redaction and references to a dedicated secret manager.
Use a project-scoped, permission-limited artifact directory and unique run identifiers instead of broad /tmp glob collection.
State that agents should only read artifacts created for the current task and should ignore unrelated files.

content.value_statement: Long projects lose decisions, blockers, and handoff details. This skill helps capture, compress, and distribute context across Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
actual_capabilities: Defines workflows for capturing key decisions, rationale, blockers, and current project state.
Provides context formats for quick summaries, full handoffs, and archived project history.
Guides multi-agent coordination through task handoff templates and artifact patterns.
Explains memory graph workflows for entities, observations, relationships, and searches.
Offers compression and progressive loading patterns to reduce context size during long tasks.
Includes troubleshooting advice for memory entities, relationships, searches, and context growth.
limitations: It is documentation and workflow guidance, not an automated context storage system.
It does not enforce secret redaction or access control for stored memory.
It assumes the user or agent has compatible memory and file tools available.
It does not resolve conflicts between agents without human review.

use_cases.title: Coordinate a Multi-Agent Build
use_cases.description: Prepare focused handoffs so reviewers, test writers, and implementers each receive relevant project state.

use_cases.title: Resume a Long Project
use_cases.description: Capture decisions, blockers, and recent changes so work can restart after a session break.

use_cases.title: Maintain Project Memory
use_cases.description: Structure entities, observations, and relationships for reusable knowledge across repeated work sessions.

prompt_templates.title: Capture Current Context
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner handoff after a short work session
prompt_templates.prompt: Capture the current task, decisions, blockers, files touched, and next steps in a concise context summary.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an Agent Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare context for the next agent. Include only goals, constraints, changed files, open questions, and risks relevant to that agent.

prompt_templates.title: Compress Project History
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced context reduction for a long task
prompt_templates.prompt: Compress the project history into quick context, full context, and archived context sections. Preserve decisions and remove repetition.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Memory Graph
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a memory graph for this project. Define entity types, relationship types, observation rules, update cadence, and cleanup rules.

output_examples.input: Capture a checkpoint after implementing authentication tests.
output_examples.output: A concise checkpoint with completed work, changed files, decisions made, remaining risks, and the next action list.

output_examples.input: Prepare context for a code review agent.
output_examples.output: A reviewer-focused handoff that highlights security concerns, performance constraints, relevant files, and review priorities.

output_examples.input: Compress three sessions of project notes.
output_examples.output: A shorter context package grouped into current goals, durable decisions, resolved issues, and archived background.

best_practices: Capture rationale with each decision so future agents understand why choices were made.
Keep handoffs scoped to the receiving agent and remove unrelated history.
Review stored memory regularly to delete outdated, duplicate, or sensitive information.
anti_patterns: Do not store credentials, tokens, or private user data in plain project memory.
Do not pass every prior message to every agent when a focused summary is enough.
Do not use shared temporary files without clear ownership, cleanup, and access boundaries.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps capture, organize, compress, and hand off context during complex AI-assisted work.

faq.question: Does it run commands or automate storage?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and templates. Any storage or tool use must be performed by the agent or user.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflows are written for general AI agent coordination and support all three tools.

faq.question: How should I handle secrets?
faq.answer: Do not store secrets in memory. Store references to approved secret managers instead.

faq.question: When should I create a checkpoint?
faq.answer: Create a checkpoint after major decisions, completed milestones, agent handoffs, or before ending a session.

faq.question: Is this useful for single-agent projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It can preserve decisions and restart context even when only one agent is involved.
